utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-98-34-T, the Prosecutor versus Naletilic and Martinovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Par, are you ready to continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Good morning. I am ready.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness AA. We shall resume -- we will take up from where we left off last week. If you remember, we were talking about Romeo Blazevic. In relation to the event that you described about Romeo Blazevic's attack on you, you said that one Ernest Takac was with him. Could you tell me, please, if at that time did you know Ernest Takac? Did you know who he was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you know his full name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not quite the -- his full name but I knew his first name. That's how things are in Mostar. It is a small place, and one meets people around town and comes across various people, so we are all familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Right. I understand. Do you know who was Ernest Takac's commander at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will the counsel and witness please make a break between question and answer? And could the witness come closer to the microphone, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Par, since you are speaking the same language, you and the witness, please do make a pause after his answer -- he answers the question. You know, Judge Diarra feels it is difficult because she relies on French to hear the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My sincere apologies, Your Honours. I will try not to do that again.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Right. So my question to you was: Did you perhaps hear at that time that Ernest Takac was a member of the 5th Battalion? Did you know that? Did you hear that at that time or didn't you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Fine. Tell us, please, did you ever hear of a unit called Mrmak?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it does ring a bell, but I wouldn't know which battalion it belonged to.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Did you know of a unit called Vinko Skrobo?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: So you heard about it? You heard about it but you don't know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it's the Vinko Skrobo was an anti-terrorist unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Do you know anything else about that unit except that you heard it was an anti-terrorist group?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew more or less that it was an anti-terrorist group and that they also manned front lines in Santic Street and manned some other front lines, but I really wouldn't know anything more about under what other unit they were or anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Very well. You said during your testimony that you heard that you more or less knew everything that was -- that you knew all the rumours in Mostar during the war, that is that you had plenty of information. Now, my question is: Did you at that time hear from someone that at that time when people were being expelled from their flats, that many soldiers and criminals misrepresented themselves, that is that they posed as Stela's soldiers? Did you hear about that, that they were doing that in order to conceal their true identity? Did you hear any such rumours?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. People who were being expelled from their towns were mostly saying that they were being expelled by Stela's and Tuta's boys.

utterances.speaker: MR. PAR
utterances.text: Right. Now I want to ask you something about the death of your mother. You showed on the photograph where she was killed, where, according to information that you have, her body was found.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Could we go into private session if we're going to talk about this, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll go to the private session

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Just a couple of questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Witness AA, this goes back to last week when you were cross-examined by Mr. Meek, the Defence counsel for Mladen Naletilic. Mr. Meek put it in cross to you that you testified in chief that you had observed that Tuta hit Pobric with the butt of a gun. Did you ever in this courtroom testify that you saw Tuta hit Pobric with the butt of a gun?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only said in my statement, as I was asked, that he did hit him, but I didn't know whether it was the butt of a gun or a Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: In fact, when I asked you that question on Wednesday in examination-in-chief, that you in fact gave the following answer:

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then he approached Pobric. Don't know what he told him, but at that moment, he suddenly hit him with the Motorola on his head and he started bleeding. And this is on page 80, line 7 of the transcript of Wednesday, 10 October. Is that what you answered on that question, Witness AA?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, on Thursday, the witness -- the counsel for Martinovic showed you an exhibit, P704.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'd like the witness to have that exhibit again. I'd like the witness to look at the front page of the exhibit, the first page of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: This exhibit was shown to you last Thursday, and could you please read out what's written -- what's written -- there are three sort of paragraphs. What's written in the middle paragraph? Could you read that out, please?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "We enclose herewith the payroll for November 1993 for the members of the Convicts Battalion and the ATG."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could we have the text put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Now, Witness, do you remember the date when you were beaten by Romeo Blazevic in the MUP station?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the evening on the 10th. It must have been around 8.00 or half past eight the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Of which month? The 10th of which month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS AA [Resumed]
utterances.text: May.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have no further questions except that I would like to tender Exhibit P12.11 as marked by the witness. And I would like to tender under seal Exhibit P752.1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Any questions from the judges?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Can I ask the Prosecutor a question about the origin of the video clip that we saw?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's taken from the Croatian Television, HTV.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Was it actually shown on television or was it footage that wasn't used?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes. It was indeed shown on television and you can ask the witness. I think he knows about this as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know that, that it was a piece of film Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. that was shown on the news? Was it accompanied with any narrative?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: I'll have to ask. I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: And if so, would it be possible for us to hear it and have a translation of what was said?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes. We can provide that to the Court but it may take --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: It may take some time. I don't want to put you on the spot. I don't want you to have to say something that you don't absolutely know. You can come back to me on that. If it was shown on television, I think the Court would like to know what the narrative was that accompanied that clip. I think the Court would like to see that clip again, to see if the emblems and the insignia on the uniforms of the soldiers who appear there could be identified, what force they belonged to. And on the clip also, it seems to me that in the line up of prisoners, we saw, or I think I saw, a prisoner who appeared to be injured about the face, and I was wondering if this witness could identify if that was the prisoner that he was describing who was hit either with the Motorola or the butt of a gun. And if we show the clip first at normal speed, because it's less distorted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We have to go to private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will go to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Are there any protective measures that you asked before for the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President and Your Honours. No. The next witness will testify in public session. Like one previous witness in this case, he is currently a prisoner in a state, and I'm going to caution the witness that he should not say where he's presently being held, but beyond that, there are no protective measures that the witness is requesting. If I could, while we're in a moment of transition, Mr. President, because the next witness is going to testify in German, we have -- with the Trial Chamber's kind permission, we understand that you've allowed or agreed that an additional OTP staff member can be present in the courtroom during the testimony of this witness. She is present. This is Marie-Ursula Kind, whom -- I believe the Trial Chamber's preference was that she sit at the counsel table, and we can make that arrangement but she's been -- among her many skills is her first language is German, and she's been of great assistance to me in preparing for this witness, and we're grateful that you've allowed her to be present in the courtroom. Mr. President, I could continue, I think, to inform the Trial Chamber of the relevant parts of the indictment that this witness will give testimony and evidence about. We believe his testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Could you tell us first who he is, which witness he is?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise, Your Honour. This is a gentleman named Falk Simang, and he is going to give evidence relevant to paragraphs 7, 10, and 11 of the indictment, which relate to the background part of the indictment. He will give evidence relevant to paragraphs 14 through 16 relating to the superior authority of the accused Mladen Naletilic. He will give evidence relevant to paragraphs 18 through 20 regarding the existence of an international armed conflict. In respect of count 1, the persecution count, he will give evidence relevant to paragraphs 25 through 27, 31 and 34. In respect of the counts 2 through 5, the counts related to forced labour, he will give evidence relevant to paragraphs 35 and 44. He will give evidence also relevant to paragraph 46, which relates to counts 11 and 12, particularly beatings, mistreatment which occurred in Sovici-Doljani area. He will give evidence relevant to paragraph 53, which is part of count 18 on forced transfer of civilians, and also paragraph 53 relating to Sovici-Doljani, paragraph 54 relating to Mostar. And finally, he will give evidence relevant to paragraphs 55 and 56, which relate to the destruction of Muslim property and the mosque in the area of Sovici-Doljani. And finally, paragraph 57, which relates to plunder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Could the usher bring the witness in, please. Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President and Your Honours. The Defence is a little confused as to why there would be Ms. Marie-Ursula Kind in the courtroom from the OTP. She's not an interpreter, and Mr. Stringer indicates that he made some agreement with the Trial Chamber to let her to sit in the courtroom. We don't know why. We haven't heard of such a thing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we received this request last Thursday asking for a member from the OTP to be present during the testimony of this witness. Her role is very limited. She's not allowed to make any interventions in the proceedings. She's just present here as a member of the OTP, so we granted this motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Witness. Would you please make the solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You may sit down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: As you can see, you have the assistance of an interpreter seated next to you, and I would ask, before we start, a couple of things. Perhaps it would be better if you could move forward a little closer to the microphones. Witness, can you please tell me your name and spell your last name for the record?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: My name is Simang, S-I-M-A-N-G. My first name is Falk, F-A-L-K.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simang, are you presently being held in custody in a prison facility in a different state outside of the Netherlands?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I want to just remind you that although we'll be referring to you by your name in the courtroom, I'd ask that you keep in mind not to tell us where you are currently being held.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Simang, were you born and raised in the city of Dresden?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: That's in the former German Democratic Republic?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And by profession, were you trained -- was your skill that of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. being a mason and a roofer?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: In approximately January of 1993, did you leave East Germany and travel to Marseille in France?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Why did you go to Marseille?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I wanted to join the Foreign Legion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were you able to join the Foreign Legion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No, I couldn't, since I had a scar from an operation which was only two months back, and for that reason I would not have passed the basic training without medical assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: When you were in Marseille, did you meet any other Germans who were also trying to join the Foreign Legion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And can you tell us the name of that person?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I unfortunately only know his first name. His first name is Jurgen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was Jurgen successful in joining the Foreign Legion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No, he was not successful. He had any problems -- he had problems with his knees, and therefore, he was requested to be back in six months' time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So did then you and Jurgen leave Marseille and travel to a different city?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what city did you travel to?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We then went from Marseille to Ljubljana and from Ljubljana to Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Approximately what month and what year did you arrive in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I suppose it was February 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was the reason why you travelled to Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We wanted to bridge the time and join as voluntary to the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Tell us what happened then when you arrived in Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We were taken to military barracks of the Croatian army. There we stayed overnight. And the next morning, we went to Zagreb. We were driven there to a hotel. There we were presented -- introduced to a number of officers, and we were told that there was no longer a war in Croatia but that they needed voluntaries in Bosnia-Herzegovina. Thus it was it happened that we were sent to Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You state that you were introduced to certain officers there. Do you know what army or military organisation they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They were officers of the Croatian army HV.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And you said that you were then sent to Bosnia-Herzegovina. Did these officers of the HV provide you with anything?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They gave us a letter, a sheet of paper, which we handed to the bus driver at the bus station, whereupon we were allowed to travel free to Bosnia-Herzegovina, to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did these officers indicate anywhere in particular where you should go in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They said we were to go to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How long did it take for you to arrive in Mostar, travelling by bus?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: A few hours. I'm not in a position, unfortunately, to tell you exactly how long it took us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So we are still talking roughly about the period sometime February 1993?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: When you arrived in Mostar, tell us what happened. Did you attempt to join an army in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. We were taken to a hotel, and in this hotel, there were some people who accompanied us. They were dressed in uniforms. We stayed overnight in that hotel. And the next morning, we were taken to the Heliodrom of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, when you say "we were taken to the Heliodrom," who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That's Jurgen and myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what happened when you arrived at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: At the Heliodrom, we came to know another German and a Croatian person who spoke fairly well German. Then we were introduced to the commanders, and we were given a room, which we could -- where we were accommodated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall who the commanders were that you were introduced to at that time?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, that was Lija and Baja.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned another German and also a Croatian person who spoke German. Do you recall their names?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, I do. The German was Maximilian Resch, and the Croatian person was Vlado. That is the only part of the name of his I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were they -- did they belong to any military organisation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. They were part of the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And within the HVO, do you know if they belonged to a particular unit?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. They were part of the ATG.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you have a conversation with the person you've named Baja, Lija?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And can you tell us what he said in that conversation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We were told that we were not supposed to play Rambo but that what it was all about was real war, and that actors, or whatever we might be called actors, were not needed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what happened after this conversation with Lija?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We had to wait for the time because we were supposed to be introduced to the general who would have the final say whether we were to be members of their groups or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And who informed you that you had to meet with a general?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We were translated by Mr. Resch or by Vlado respectively.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you that question again. You said that you were informed that you had to wait or you had to be introduced to the general who would have the final say. Let me first ask you: Who told you that you had to be introduced to the general?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: It was told or it was said by Lija, and it was translated by Vlado.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And did you subsequently learn who was the general that he referred to?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. We were told that the general's name was Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you learn anything else about Tuta at that time?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Not in the beginning, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll ask the witness be shown Exhibit 41. It consists of two photographs. Mr. President, I have copies here at counsel table. If it would speed things along, we could just work with those for the time being.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. And it will be put on the ELMO, I suppose?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Perhaps the witness could first take a quick look at those and then we'll put them on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And as the usher puts those on the ELMO - either one is fine; we will put them both on one after the other - witness, can you tell us if you recognise the person whose photographs were just placed in front of you?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. That's the commander of the ATG, Lija.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is this the person that you've just referred to?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, that's him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If you could place the other photograph there for a moment or two? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simang, after this particular meeting at the Heliodrom, did you have an opportunity to see this person at other times?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. I saw him frequently at a later stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we can withdraw the photographs now. So then you said that you were to be introduced to this -- the general who would decide. Did that meeting then subsequently take place?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, it did happen.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Approximately one or two days later, we were taken up from the Heliodrom to Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Tell us what happened when you arrived in Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We went to a cafe, Cafe Marlboro by name, and there we were introduced to General Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How did you communicate with General Tuta?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Astonishingly in German, because General Tuta knows German perfectly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was anyone else present with him at the Cafe Marlboro, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, several people, all dressed in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you subsequently learn the identity of any of those other people?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, I did. One of them was Ivan, his driver and his bodyguard.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did anyone accompany you to Siroki Brijeg from Mostar?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, this German person, Maximilian Resch, did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And was Jurgen also with you? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. As a matter of fact, Jurgen was also present.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How was Tuta dressed at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: He was dressed in a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what was said by you and by Tuta when you met with him there?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Tuta asked us whether we had military training. We answered to the affirmative. And then Tuta told us that we were not here for fun.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, when you told Tuta that you had military training, were you telling him the truth?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No. I didn't have any pre-military training by that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you recall anything else that was said at this meeting?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No, not so far.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What took place after this meeting occurred?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: General Tuta gave sort of a sheet of paper to Maximilian Resch, where he wrote something onto this piece of paper, and then we went back to the Heliodrom, to Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know what was written on this sheet of paper? What was it about?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. Later we were -- said that we had been accepted.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So then after you had this meeting with Tuta, you said that you went back to the Heliodrom in Mostar. What happened then back at the Heliodrom?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We were sent to the office of Lija via respectively a form -- a sheet of paper with a form was laid before us on the table. Vlado translated it and all our personal data were recorded. That was more or less our acceptance to the group.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you receive any supplies or equipment then after you did this paperwork?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. Later we went up to Siroki Brijeg again to a sort of store or magazine where we were handed over a uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, at the time that you were doing the paperwork in Mostar, did anyone tell you about any rules that applied to your joining?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. We were still told down there that we were in an army, that the laws of the army of the war were valid here, that we would be shot in case of desertion, and that we had to stick to the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, at this point when you were at the Heliodrom, what group or army did you think you were joining? What was your understanding?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: In the beginning, we thought that we were part of the ATG down at the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then did that change at some point?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. We were then placed to the Park Hotel at Siroki Brijeg, and there we were assigned to the Kaznjenicka Bojna.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, a moment ago I think you were starting -- I had asked you about military supplies or equipment that you received. Where did you receive those?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: At Siroki Brijeg, at our base that was almost opposite to the Marlboro cafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What sorts of things did you then receive in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Uniform, that is, a shirt, boots, trousers, a sweater, and a jacket.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At any point did you receive an identification card?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, we did, an army ID. When we were dressed in uniform, we were sent to a photographer to have our photographs taken, whereupon an Iskaznica, that's an army ID, was prepared.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At this time I'd ask the witness be shown a new exhibit which has been marked 354.1.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, you've just been handed two pieces of paper, and can you tell us if you recognise what's been placed before you?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. That's an army ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us when and how that was made?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: When? Well, it was then when we had taken our photographs. Then the photographs were sent in. And how it is prepared, I do not know. I only know that the papers were sent away and that a few weeks later we received this ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Simang, looking at the identification, it appears to be dated 27th of April, 1993. Are you able to explain the time difference between what I thought was February 1993, this being dated April 1993?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We had to wait for some time for the IDs to be returned. We were said time and again that the IDs had been sent in and that it would take some time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And so do you recognise this as an ID card that you received?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, correct, that's my ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you testified that you were informed, in fact, that you would be assigned to the Kaznjenicka Bojna, the Convicts Battalion. Where was the Convicts Battalion based?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Our accommodation was Siroki Brijeg, Park Hotel, and the base was approximately five minutes to walk on foot, opposite the Cafe Marlboro, also located at Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, we are talking about, I believe, February of 1993. Tell us, from that point forward -- from that point forward, how long did you remain a member of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Up to the time when I left Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall when that was?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Approximately February, March, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At the time that you left, was the conflict between the Muslims and the Croats still going on?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No. At that time, United Nations were there, and it was said that foreign soldiers had to leave Croatia or they, as an alternative, could -- should get married.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll ask the witness be shown Exhibit 26.11, which is a photograph, if it could be placed on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simang, do you recognise the photograph that's now been placed on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. That's our accommodation. That's where we stayed overnight there. That's the Hotel Park at Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And how long did you live at this place?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: For the whole of the period.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And during that period, what rank or position did you hold in the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I was an ordinary soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us generally what sorts of tasks you were assigned to perform during military operations of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Several times, I was sent to the infantry. Then I was sent to cannon, to Mr. Resch. It differed, depending on the assignment we were sent out for.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How were you paid?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We got our money from the base that was opposite the Cafe Marlboro, and we were given approximately 350, 400 deutschmarks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Is that per month?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Per month, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, again, generally speaking, during this period, February 1993 until the time you left the Convicts Battalion, tell us, as far as you know, how the Convicts Battalion was organised. What was its structure?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: In the Convicts Battalion, there were almost exclusively officers. They were subordinate to our commander; our commander was Mario Cikota. And above all of them was Tuta. Tuta was the one who had the last, decisive say.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were subordinates of -- were other soldiers based in other places outside of Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, they were, for certain actions. A mortar unit was called from Posusje, from Ljubuski, but also from Grude and also from Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You said earlier that Lija was the commander of the anti-terrorist group or ATG. What is ATG?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: ATG is an anti-terrorist group, and it was part and parcel of the Convicts Battalion. It was subordinate to the supreme command of General Tuta, and so also were Lija and Baja.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did General Tuta have any superiors, as far as you knew?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Not that I would be aware of. Maybe, perhaps in Zagreb, but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'd ask the witness be shown Exhibit 26.9.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Witness, are you able to recognise this place which appears on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No, I'm sorry, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If I could ask the usher perhaps just to give the photograph to the witness and allow him to take a moment just to look at it, to see if he can recognise anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, are you able to recognise this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That is Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If we could place it back on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, let me ask you first, you mentioned the Cafe Marlboro. Is the Cafe Marlboro shown in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. It should be on the -- on the bottom left, the house bottom left.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If the witness perhaps could use the pointer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simang, if you can -- and if it would assist you just to hold the photograph for a moment again, just let us know.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: At this part there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, are you --

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That obviously was our base and there, just opposite the Marlboro Cafe. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So just for the record, is the Marlboro Cafe shown in its entirety on this photograph?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I cannot tell you exactly whether it's exactly this house. I only know that it was just a bit opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to ask if the witness could be given a marker.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simang, I'm going to ask you to place a circle in the area in which you're indicating would be the location of the Cafe Marlboro. And, Witness, while you've got the pen, you've just mentioned that your base was there, and so I'm going to ask you also --

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I'm no longer sure. I'm sorry. I'm no longer sure when I look at this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. We can set the photograph aside then. We can withdraw the photograph. Now, during the time that you were a member of the Convicts Battalion, tell us generally what was the daily routine, if there was a daily routine there in Siroki Brijeg for members of the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. We had to come to the base in the morning. There was a sort of roll call, where we were instructed what sort of stage there was, green, yellow, or red, whether we were allowed to leave Siroki Brijeg or whether we had to be dressed in army uniform at the Park Hotel. And then we were mostly sent to the fitness centre in Siroki Brijeg. There we made jogging and were trained in keeping ourselves fit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was the difference between stage green, yellow, or red?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: When we had green, we were allowed to leave Siroki Brijeg. The yellow phase meant we had to stay at Siroki Brijeg, and red meant that in full gear, including the rifle, we had to be in front of the cafe. That was when an assignment was imminent.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You mentioned a roll call. Who would do the roll call?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: It depended. Sometimes General Tuta was there with us or Ivan Andabak or our commander, Mario Cikota.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who was Ivan Andabak?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Ivan Andabak was General Tuta's right-hand man or his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was his role in the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: He was the deputy of General Tuta. Most of the time he then was in the Ministry at Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What languages did he speak?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Perfectly German, as far as I know, Spanish, and Serbo-Croatian.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever have occasion to see him using his Spanish language skills?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. He was in touch with the Spanish UNPROFOR who were there or who had their headquarters in Medjugorje, and there he talked to people occasionally.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know if Andabak ever received a promotion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. General Andabak was promoted general.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall when that occurred generally?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That was towards the end of the war. It must have been early 1994, but I could not exactly tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who promoted him to the rank of general?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That was direct orders from Zagreb.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And how do you know that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Because there was a ceremony and this Susak was also present, the Minister of Defence, who also is of origin from Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Where did the ceremony take place?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The promotion was in Park Hotel, and then we went up to Kitic. That was the restaurant where the actual celebrations took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was this in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, it was there too.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You mentioned that -- you mentioned also the name of someone named Cikota. Who is Cikota?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: He was the commander of the Convicts Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was his position in the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: He was our commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who was superior to him in the chain of command?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Ivan Andabak and General Tuta.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, is it a convenient time for us to break?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, it is, Mr. President. I apologise. I didn't see the clock.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will resume at 11.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Simang, during the time that you were a member of the Convicts Battalion, did the Convicts Battalion participate in any military operations in a place called Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, they did, in Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And did you participate in any of those military operations yourself?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, I participated.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How many times were you involved in operations in Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Approximately two or three times.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you recall approximately what month these operations took place?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I do not know, as far as time schedules are concerned. What I know is my first operation was when Cikota fell, and obviously it is known here when that was, as far as the time, the point of time is concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you're saying that the first operation in Doljani was the one in which Cikota was killed?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me ask you some questions, then, about the operation that occurred there prior to or at the time Cikota was killed. First, let me ask, if you know, what was the objective of this first operation at Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The Muslim troops had made an attack. They displaced the front lines. And it was our job to make the -- to go back to the old line, front lines, and also to attack a bunker.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know how many members of the Convicts Battalion were deployed in this operation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The entire Convicts Battalion and the entire ATG.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: When you say the ATG, are you able to identify a particular ATG?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: From Heliodrom, the ATG from Heliodrom, Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And again, who was the commander of that particular ATG?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The ATG was under the command of Lija and Baja, and the supreme commander was General Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you and other members of the Convicts Battalion go directly from Siroki Brijeg to Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No, not directly to Doljani. We had a stop in between, somewhere in between, at a place called Masna Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What did you do at Masna Luka and how long did you stay there?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: In Masna Luka we just stayed overnight. We were given ammunition, and we waited for being able to march into Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was your own task in this operation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I was -- I participated in this operation, in cleansing this town of Doljani, and also at the bunker position.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The English word that I just received is "cleansing." Tell us what you mean by "cleansing."

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That the Muslim population be driven away from the place of Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Tell us how you participated in that task.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We searched houses for people who might still have been in these houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what was done with persons who were found in those houses?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They were driven from this place. Few were in the church, that's in the mosque, of this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned also something about taking a bunker. What -- can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The bunker was the job of Cikota, and in this operation, where he fell, some person must have been outside this bunker, and with a targeted firing, our commander, Cikota, was killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How did you learn that he was killed?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How did you personally learn that Cikota had been killed in this operation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I was approximately 100 metres away from this spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, did -- was any base or headquarters established for this Doljani operation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you describe this place?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: It was some sort of farmyard with a fish basin or fish growing, whatever it meant. It was some sort of courtyard.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibits 8.8, 8.9, and 8.10. If the witness could first look at those and then we'll place them one after another on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, that's this base.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. We're talking about all three photographs. Is it your testimony that they show this base that you've just described?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Correct, yes. That's the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: For the record, Exhibit 8.8 has now been placed on the ELMO. I'd ask that Exhibit 8.9 be placed there. Now Exhibit 8.10. We will come back to those, so I think they can be left there. We don't need them on the ELMO at this point, but there will be additional questions about one of those photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you just talked about when Cikota was killed in this operation. Tell us then what happened after that occurred.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The body of Cikota was brought back to the base and then General Tuta ordered that the complete ATG and the Convicts Battalion were to withdraw to Siroki Brijeg for the funeral.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So did any further military operations take place at that time in Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Nobody returned to Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How long were you in Doljani, you personally, how long were you in Doljani before Cikota was killed?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Our commander fell on the first day of our assignment in Doljani. Before that we were in Masna Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, during this day, this operation, do you know if any Muslims were captured in Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And do you know what happened to them?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They were brought for interrogation to the base and there General Tuta and Ivan Andabak interrogated them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: When you say "the base," are you talking about the photographs that you were just looking at?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Correct. That's what I'm talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were any prisoners removed from Doljani and taken to a different town during that first operation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. There was a transport that was supposed to go to Ljubuski.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, did you personally participate in that transport to Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I had participated in one transport, but I do not know whether it's the one we're talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you stated that the Convicts Battalion withdrew and returned to Siroki Brijeg for the funeral. Were you present in Siroki Brijeg when the funeral of Cikota took place?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, I was present, and I wore a wreath.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How many days did the Convicts Battalion remain in Siroki Brijeg for the funeral of Cikota?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I am sorry, but I wouldn't be able to give you the exact length of time. A few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then after those few days, what did the Convicts Battalion do?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We returned to Masna Luka and then to Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what was the purpose of going back to Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: To take revenge for the killing of Cikota.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, what were your orders in respect of that second operation at Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Complete cleansing and no prisoners to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How did you receive those orders?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: This order was given down at the base, and we were translated it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who personally gave you that order?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: General Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were those orders carried out during this operation in Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, during what we are now calling the second operation at Doljani, were any Muslim prisoners captured at that time?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. A few were taken prisoner. It was a number of people dressed in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what was done, then, with those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They were also interrogated down at the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know whether those prisoners were mistreated in any way?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. They were beaten.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'd ask the witness be shown Exhibit 8.9 again, which is one of the photographs he just looked at.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, looking again, for the record, what is this place that we are looking at here?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That's the main base of the operation for Doljani. This is where General Tuta was based.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were any other commanders of the Convicts Battalion based in this location?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. Ivan Andabak was also represented there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You were describing beatings that took place at this location. Perhaps if you could use the pointer, you could indicate the location where the beatings were occurring.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Approximately here, there was a wooden shed, a wooden shed which is no longer existing there in this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was taking place at the wooden shed?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The prisoners were taken there. Then General Tuta and Ivan Andabak came and interrogated the people one after another.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to go through this event in greater detail. Were prisoners beaten before Tuta and Andabak arrived?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who was beating the prisoners at that time?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: First the people who had arrested them. They had to crawl on their knees and hands to the shed. There they were kicked with the feet and they were beaten with the butts of rifles in their backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you participate in the beating of the prisoners at that time?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You said that they were crawling. What was the ground like in that area?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: At that time, it was very muddy. It had rained.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How many prisoners, approximately, were in your custody there on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: It was approximately six to seven people, but I'm not entirely sure about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How long did these beatings take place before Tuta and Andabak arrived?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to tell you for how long it had taken place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you give an approximation? Are we talking about several hours, or some shorter period of time?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, I cannot tell you what distance they had covered before they were taken prisoner. They had been taken prisoner in a forest place, and then it was a distance of 10 to 15 minutes to be taken to our base. And when they arrived at our base, General Tuta and Andabak joined us approximately five minutes later.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So just so we are clear, you were not present in the place where these people were captured?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I personally was not present when they were taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, taking the pointer again would you please indicate the location in which these beatings were taking place before the arrival of Tuta and Andabak?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They came from this forest behind the house. So they moved then this distance and arrived then at this place, and it was here at this spot that this wooden shed was located.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simang, at this time taking a marker, if you would please place a number 1 to indicate the location where the prisoners were crawling through the mud and being beaten.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, crawling through the mud, and here in front. So it was at this spot where the wooden shed must have been located.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like for you to put a -- before you give the photo back to the usher, please put a number 2 at the location of the wooden shed.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, tell us what then occurred after Tuta and Andabak arrived.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Then the beating of the prisoners was stopped and then each of the prisoners, one after another, had to go into the shed and there they were interrogated by General Tuta and Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, at some point while these interrogations were taking place, did a different group of people arrive?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, during the interrogations, no group did come, but then a group of vehicles from UNPROFOR came.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Again perhaps using the photograph and the pointer, could you indicate where they came from or where they became apparent to you and the others who were at that headquarters?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That was where the vehicle parked.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps you could put a number 3 at that location.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So what occurred when these UNPROFOR people showed up?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Ivan Andabak talked to them and then they went off again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And after they left -- well, let me first ask you, while they were there, what was happening with the prisoners while these UNPROFOR people were present?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Nothing. Nobody touched them during that time. They were standing next to the shed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever learn what the UNPROFOR people were told by Andabak?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No. That's not known to me. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Then after the UNPROFOR people left, what happened?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The prisoners were led into the wood behind the shed, and what happened to the prisoners afterwards, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Let me first ask you about interrogations. How many of the prisoners were interrogated?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: All of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who interrogated them?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: General Tuta and Ivan Andabak.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know if they were mistreated during the interrogations?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I was not present. I heard them shouting, screaming, not more.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you've indicated that the prisoners were led into the woods behind the shed. When did that occur?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: After UNPROFOR had disappeared.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who led them into the woods?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: A few comrades from my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know why they did that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were any orders given in respect of those prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I was not given any orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you hear others being given orders?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I haven't heard anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What happened after those prisoners were led into the woods?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, I must object to this line of questioning. It's been asked and answered. More than five minutes ago, this witness has testified that he was not there, that he does not know what happened, that UNPROFOR came, that these prisoners were gone into the woods. He did not know. Now he's even further answered. He didn't hear anything. He didn't hear any orders. And I object to this line of questioning. It's bordering on leading and subjective, but it's been asked and answered, and that's my objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your objection is not so for the previous one. The previous one is what happened after those prisoners were led into the woods. Yes, Mr. Stringer. You may continue to ask this question. We want to know what happened after those prisoners were led into the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you see what happened to those prisoners after they were led into the woods?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No, I did not see what happened in the woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you hear what happened in the woods?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I heard shooting, firings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Where was the shooting coming from?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: From that place in the woods where the prisoners were taken to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you see anyone come out of the woods subsequently?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Our people from the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Which people are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Who previously had gone into the woods with the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How long were they in the woods?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I'm sorry, a few minutes. I did not look at my watch.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What did those soldiers do after they returned from the woods?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They replenished their magazines, that's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know why they replenished their magazines?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: He can't answer that. He's already said he doesn't know what happened. We are asking him to speculate. All he can say is what he saw. I think you can take it that the bench will draw inferences. We can't ask him to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Very well. Your Honour, if I may say, I asked the witness does he know why. And I will withdraw the question but I think that in first asking him if he knows, then it gives him an opportunity to say whether or not he does know why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: If he knows, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simang, can you tell us, if you know, why then did they replenish their magazines?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, I cannot tell you. They were empty. I do not know whether they had lost or shot out the ammunition.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, during this second operation in Doljani that we are talking about, you've been talking about Muslim prisoners. Perhaps we should clarify. Were those prisoners soldiers or civilians?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They were -- they wore uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know which army they belonged to?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Part of the Muslim army. The army patches were lilies.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, were any civilians, particularly Muslim civilians, present in Doljani during this operation after the funeral of Cikota?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I have not understood. During the funeral of Cikota?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I will ask the question again. After the funeral of Cikota, after the Convicts Battalion returned to Doljani, did you find any Muslim civilians in the village?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. There were still Muslim civilians in the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how the civilians -- first of all, how were you able to identify persons as being civilians?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They were seated there without any uniforms. It was old women, children, and very old men.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How were the civilians treated?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They were driven out of the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And why were they driven out from the mosque?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Because the mosque was to be blown up.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Why was the mosque going to be blown up?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Because it was a Muslim house of God.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you receive an order regarding the mosque?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I was not given any order.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was done with the mosque? What happened to it?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Whether it was destroyed finally, I would not know. I was only present when the explosives were attached to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who attached explosives to the mosque?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: A few soldiers from our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you hear the explosion of the mosque?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No. I cannot tell you whether it was blown up finally.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: These soldiers who placed explosives there, why did they do that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, I assume because they had planned to destroy the mosque.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you see -- well, were any houses in Doljani damaged at that time?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. Unexpectedly, all Muslim houses were set to fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you receive any orders in respect of the Muslim houses?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I was not given any order.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Are you aware of any orders that were carried out?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I do not know whether orders were fulfilled. I only know that the houses were set to fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were the soldiers doing this on their own?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Meek.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEEK
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object strenuously. This calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I agree with Mr. Meek. It is kind of speculation in this aspect. Can you escape this question?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simang, were you present when houses were burned?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, I was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And who was participating in the burning of the houses?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Comrades from our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And which unit is that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Kaznjenicka Bojna and ATG.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: Mr. Stringer, I think sometimes you treat the Bench as if we're children. You know we know all this. We know that now, there were no orders that he knows of. We know that soldiers that belong to this battalion. We know what battalion he belongs to. We know that the houses were burnt down. We got that awhile ago. Can we move on?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: You can assume that we have some intelligence and that we've picked up the point. It doesn't have to be spelled out to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I apologise. Believe me, I don't believe that the Trial Chamber has any deficiencies along those lines.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: We can move faster because we picked it up the very first time. This is a very good witness. He answers what he knows.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At the time the houses were burned or prior to, were they being used for any military purpose?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No, it's not known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How did the members of the Convicts Battalion know which houses were Muslim houses?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: There were still Croatian inhabitants in the village, and they had told us which houses were occupied by the Muslim population, and then a few people from our units were born in this place or they knew this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was done with houses of Croats at this time?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Croat houses were not touched.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was anything done with other property of Muslims in the village?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, what was of value we have taken along. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What sorts of things were taken?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, what you could take along, what you could carry. For instance, a chain-saw, new porcelain objects, or anything else which brought some value when being sold.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Where was Tuta while this was taking place, if you know?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: He was at the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The base in Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did he see -- was he present when this looting was taking place?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: He personally did not loot.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was he present or was he aware that others were looting?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: He has seen that we had loaded our trucks with things, but he was not present. He was at the base.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And was he in a position also to see Muslim houses burning?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. One could see this very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was -- I may have asked this before. If I did, I apologise. The mosque in Doljani, was it used for any military purpose?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: By us or what do you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: By anyone.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was the mosque used for?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, it was the place where the old people from the village had withdrawn, I suppose for protection.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. How many -- how long did you and the other members of the Convicts Battalion remain in Doljani on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I'm really sorry. I do not know how many days we were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simang, do you know if any members of the Convicts Battalion received any sorts of awards or recommendations, recognition, I should say, in connection with the operation in Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No. It's not known to me whether some people were given reward for the operation at Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. I didn't ask about a reward. I was asking more in terms of recognition in an official capacity.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: There was an official recognition, but to my knowledge, it is not a recognition for an operation at Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Simang, I'd like to change the topic and ask you now if you and other members of the Convicts Battalion participated in any military operations in the city of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. There were several actions at or in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And before we start talking about those -- I will just go directly to the first, the first operation which you can recall [no microphone], the first time you participated in an operation in Mostar. Are you able to tell us roughly when that occurred?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there is no mike. There must be some problem. Can you try it again, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simang, I'll just ask you again. The first time, the first operation in Mostar, can you tell us approximately what month that took place?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The first operation at Mostar was the beginning of the war between Croats and Muslims, but I cannot tell you exactly which month it was. It could have been March, April, 1993, approximately, but I do not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Describe for us what this first operation -- what occurred and what was your task?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We were called to our base at Siroki Brijeg opposite Cafe Marlboro. Then roll call took place, and then we were told that down at Mostar, at Heliodrom, a vehicle of our soldiers had been fired at, and then we had to take a response action. And then at 5.00 in the morning, it was still dark, I was assigned to Maximilian Resch Bofors. We looked for a position or at least we were assigned a position from which we had to fire. And I do not know when the order came. At least it was dark when all barrels fired at the other side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Let me ask you some questions about that. You -- first of all, starting with the last part of what you just said, you said, "It was dark and all barrels were fired at the other side." Can you be more specific? What's the location that was being fired into?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We were at the serpentines to the direction of Mostar, and we took aim over the Neretva, not at this side where the Croatian population was but at the other side of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And you said it was still dark. Did the attack begin while it was still dark?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. The attack was started in darkness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what weapon were you using?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I was at a 40 millimetre cannon called Bofors.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know what other sorts of weapons were used in this operation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Several Bofors were used. There were still people from Posusje who had joined. Then BPR, that is mortars, were placed in positions, and heavy machine-guns.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
