utterances.text: You said that you were firing into the other side. Again, I just want to be very clear, if you can tell us, what side of Mostar, geographically, were you firing into?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I cannot tell you east or west because I usually mix it up. I know that we shot across the Neretva, and later, the Muslim population was let over the Neretva, or driven over it. That is we -- that is practically we shot at what was later the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you have specific targets in that Muslim side?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No. We didn't have any specific targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, as time went on that day, did -- were you given other targets to fire at?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. When it became bright, other targets were named to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How were you informed of those other targets?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Through a Motorola, that is through radio.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And with whom did you speak on the Motorola?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We were announced it by General Tuta over Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: At that point, what targets did you give you?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Targets were -- there were MG nests, or from where our people were fired at, from the direction of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How long did this operation last?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: It was wound up approximately at noon or early in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know where Tuta was located while this attack was taking place?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I do not know the exact place.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know what town he was in?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. Siroki Brijeg or Mostar, but I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Could you communicate from Mostar to Siroki Brijeg by Motorola?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. Through radio you could be in touch when you were in the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know where the ministry was located?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, I can only say at the main roads, when you went down Mostar from Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just to be clear, do you know in what city or town this ministry that you're referring to was located?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Mostar is the name of the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know what was the objective of this attack on Mostar that you've just described?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, it was a revenge action, because a bus of ours had been fired at, who was part and parcel of the ATG or the Heliodrom.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Simang, I'd like to ask you some questions about other military operations that occurred in Mostar. What was the next operation that you can recall?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We marched into Mostar. And I do not know, eastern or western side, we cleansed the entire side after all troops had been massed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Are you able to tell us again approximately when this occurred?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I assume at the beginning of the war, March or April 1993. Unfortunately, I'm not in a position to give you the exact time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. You said that the objective or that you cleansed the entire side after troops had been massed there. Tell us what do you mean by cleansing the entire side?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, we have driven people from their houses and from their flats, and then they were put together in various accommodations from where, later on, they were transported to different places.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: From whom did you receive your instructions about what to do that day?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I was assigned to a group of Croats because the Bofors could not be used, and these exact orders to me were given by General Tuta. So he said which group I should belong to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The people who were driven from their houses, can you tell us generally what group that belonged to?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. It was Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And what were your instructions in terms of what to do with those Muslims?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We had thronged them together in a gymnasium place, and from there they were then shipped off. The majority of them, because we had only a small portion of them, the majority of them were placed in the stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, this operation that you're describing in Mostar, can you tell us approximately how long it lasted? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: It was a few days.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Where did you stay at night during this operation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: In the evenings, we mostly drove back to Siroki Brijeg, and early in the morning we returned back.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did other members of the Convicts Battalion participate in this operation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. All units who were under General Tuta's order, plus from the HV a group, but I cannot tell you the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And just to be clear, you said the "HV." What unit are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: HV is the Croatian army.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How were you able to recognise members of the Croatian army?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They had patches. On our patches was "HVO," and the Croatian army had HV patches.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know what actions the HV members were doing in Mostar at that time?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They had the same objectives as we had.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know who was the commander of the Croatian army units which were present?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was General Praljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you see General Praljak in Mostar at that time?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. One morning when we picked up our ribbons. That was these ribbons to recognise each other. We changed these ribbons every morning, and when we collected them, that was in a restaurant at Mostar. It was there when General Tuta, General Praljak, and two more people were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you have an idea roughly how many soldiers combined participated in this operation which you've been describing?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No. I would not be able to tell you, but I think it was quite an enormous number.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How were you able to locate Muslims who were driven out of their homes?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, I personally could not differentiate. That's the people from our unit who came more or less from Mostar. So most of them came from there. And then in these high-rise buildings, the locals drew our attention that there were such people living there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simang, could you describe for us if there is a typical example of how one of these cleansing events took place? How did you actually drive the people out of their homes?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, I participated in it, and the others from our group, they had given orders in the Croatian language. I do not know Croatian so well that I would understand each word. So they went out, and it was in groups that we brought them to this gymnasium hall. That was not very far away from the ministry, in a complex of buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Was it ever necessary to use force in order to accomplish this task?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, what does "force" mean? Some kicks with a butt, but otherwise everything went quite smoothly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you see any Muslims mistreated during this operation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I do not know "mistreated." I do not know what you're alluding to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were any beatings -- did any beatings occur?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. I just said that occasionally, a kick with a butt.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll ask the witness -- let me first ask you, Mr. Simang, during this operation, did you communicate with Tuta?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Personally, I did not have any contact with General Tuta during this operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I'll ask the witness be shown Exhibit number 36, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE CLARK
utterances.text: While you're doing that, Mr. Stringer, can I ask you to do something? This witness has said on a number of occasions that he's not good on dates, and he thinks that this was -- this event which he's describing, or series of events, took place during the early days of the conflict between the Croats and the Muslims. Just to help us to see if he's describing other events which have been described, could you ask him if he can remember whether these events took place after the events in Doljani and after the death of General Cikota - or sorry, he may not have been a general but certainly a commander - and then perhaps we could see it in context.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simang, before we go to the photograph, let me ask you about that. You've described already the events in Doljani in which your commander, Cikota, was killed. The events that you're now describing in Mostar, do you know if that occurred before or after the events in Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That was the beginning of the war, that is prior to the death of Cikota.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So you associate the attack you're now describing as being the beginning of the war, if you will?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. If the witness could now be shown Exhibit number 36.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. Simang, have you had an opportunity to look at the photograph that's been marked Exhibit 36?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I want to ask you, with the pointer, and then I'm going to ask you to place some marks on this photograph, if you recognise any of the people who are shown in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, first of all, I would not want this to be interpreted to the witness. I intervened because this text is in the Croatian language, so my colleague Mr. Meek does not understand this. And also I would like to ask kindly that what I'm about to say right now not be interpreted to the witness because it's very important. Your Honours --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Your request is granted. We will not interpret what you're going to say into German. Or you want him to leave for a minute?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: You want him to leave?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: I think I would agree with counsel. I think that, at the very least, if we are not going to translate for the witness, we should inform him explicitly that we are not going to translate, rather than just moving ahead without him, but I think the best solution is to have him removed from the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We will have the witness removed from the courtroom for a few minutes. The usher will show you out of the room.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Should I stay here, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: No, you may go with the witness. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. So first and foremost, that's the newspaper and that's the photograph that we have been discussing, if you remember, a few days ago, and with regard to the identification of General Andabak, and that is what the Prosecutor said then, that this was his source of information. It's a newspaper, and he's showing it now as a newspaper. And also there is a caption underneath the photograph saying exactly who it is on this photograph. Of course, you don't understand the first few words, but if you look at the rest, you will see there is General Praljak, Vukovic and Andabak. The names are all there. And to give this kind of a photograph to a witness in order to identify someone, and then underneath there is a caption where it's all stated quite clearly, I mean -- I think, Your Honour, that this is unfair to the Defence and unjust, and I don't think that this should be shown to the witness at all, this photograph with this caption. And after that, I'm going to ask the Prosecutor to say whether this is the Globus newspaper. That was the basis of my objection the last time. And I'm afraid that I worked to the detriment of my client then, and if I did, I did so because I have been asking from the very outset this honourable Trial Chamber to give the Defence more time. We still haven't had enough time to study all the 17 binders that were served upon us. Also, until the present day, we did not get the translations of all these documents, or also of the correspondence between this particular witness and the Office of the Prosecutor. We got that correspondence a year ago, and we did not get a translation of that correspondence, so I did not manage to discuss it with my client. I did not manage to have it translated. I would have paid for it myself. I have been doing a lot of things from my own pocket here. However, that is a subject that can be dealt with on some other occasion. But I was told that this photograph from the newspaper that we have in front of us and that we have seen, that it was a different source of information. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have to deal with the matters one by one. I know that you raised this same issue you have mentioned just a few days before, on the admission of the documents into the evidence, and so far, to my knowledge, this Exhibit P36 has been already admitted into Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. evidence. And in fairness to your client, we could ask this photograph be redacted, that is to redact the captions and the content of this newspaper, just so that we have the photograph alone. Is that proper way out in this case? Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We will redact the photograph over the lunch break. I'll leave it for now and come back to it with the direct examination after the lunch break, after the photograph has been redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Are we going to continue with this witness or we will break at this minute?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We are in your hands on that, Mr. President. I can work with the witness up until 1.00 or we can break at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we'll break right now, but we might start earlier. We will start at 2.20 in the afternoon, ten minutes earlier. --- Luncheon recess taken at 12.50 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer. Did you prepare the photo? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We've redacted all the text of the article, and we can distribute those at this time, and I'll ask that -- after it's been distributed, if it could be also shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Simang, looking at this photograph, I'd like you to tell us if you recognise any of the people whose faces appear in that photograph.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What are the names of the people that you recognise?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: General Tuta, Ivan Andabak, and General Praljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: If you could take a pen, I'm going to ask you to place a circle around the heads of each of the persons you've just mentioned. A circle.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And now while you've got the marker in your hand, place a number 1 next to the person you're calling General Tuta.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: A number 2 above the circle of the person you're calling Andabak?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And number 3 around the person or by the circle of the person you're calling Praljak.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we can place that on the ELMO. Now, Mr. Simang, this person Praljak, if you could just tell us again where you saw this person.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That was in Mostar where we had an operation, and there he was down there in a cafe when we picked up our ribbons, our recognition ribbons.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. And that's something that you mentioned already earlier today in your testimony; is that right?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know in respect of that Mostar operation what was the position of Mr. Praljak?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Unfortunately, I wouldn't be able to say. I assume that he ordered his troops in coordination with General Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You said "his troops." What troops are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Those of the HV.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: This person Praljak, did you see him on any other occasions?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever see him in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No, neither did I see him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Before the lunch break, you were testifying about an operation in Mostar in which you were driving people from their homes. And again, just so we're clear, what people or group of people are we talking about who were driven from their homes?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What kind of places were they living in? Where were these people found?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, in their houses and in their flats.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You say "their flats." What do you mean by that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Sort of flats in high-rise buildings.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, during this operation, what was done with Croat inhabitants whom you encountered?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Nothing happened to these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Because they were Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who was in command of this operation which you've been describing?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, the supreme commander for us was General Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know where he was located during this operation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: In the ministry.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And again, what town or city was the ministry located in?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: In Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: During this operation, were there any Muslims who resisted leaving their flats?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, nothing is known to me. At least in those cases where I was present, nobody objected.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: During this operation, did you attempt to distinguish between civilians and Muslim soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Why not?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, we were not explained to make any distinction.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know why the civilians were forced from their homes on that day in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: It's not known to me, but I assume so that there was a quiet situation down in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, after the Muslims were removed from their homes and their flats, what happened to their property that was inside those places?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, the same as in Doljani. What we could carry away, we took it away as our property.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were any of your commanding officers aware that this was taking place?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And why do you say that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Because they have seen so. We have loaded things on to the Bofors and on to our cars.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, when we talk about commanders, who are we talking about that knew about the taking of property?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: General Tuta, Ivan Andabak and Cikota.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: To your knowledge, were any members of the Convicts Battalion ever punished for taking the property of Muslims from Mostar?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No. Nothing is known to me that a person would have been punished for taking along Muslim property.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you've just said that during this operation, you believe Tuta was located at the ministry in Mostar. Did you ever see him there?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And now I'm talking about these days of this Mostar operation that you've been describing.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you see him there with any prisoners?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: We can take a pause, if you like.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: It's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you need some water? Can you tell us what happened to the prisoners who were at the ministry that you've described?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: A group was led to the place. They were standing, one next to each other, in a row. They were surrounded by our people. They had to show their hands in front of them. Then it became hectic and loud, and the General Tuta took his pistol and shot one of the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: First let me start by asking you if you [no microphone] -- let me first ask you to describe this group of prisoners you're talking about now. How many people and what kind of people were they?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: It was men, women and, as far as I remember, one child was also there.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How were they dressed?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, ordinary, plain cloth. One had army boots on, army boots. And otherwise, they were normally plain-clothed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What was your position as you were observing this? How far away were you?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: How far away? I could not tell exactly in metres but I was -- well, immediately encircling them together with the rest of our people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you said that they had to show their hands. Do you know why they had to do that? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: As I was reported, one of them obviously had an imprint of a hand grenade on one of his fingers and that's why they had to show their hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you said that you saw Tuta take his pistol and shoot one of the prisoners. Can you please describe for us exactly what you saw as you recall that today?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, as I said, they had to show their hands. Then it was loud. Tuta was shouting something in Croatian language. Then he drew his pistol and shot a person dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Where did he shoot him? In what part of his body was this person shot?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: In the person's head.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What happened next?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The same action repeated -- was repeated after two or three people further down, but this time not with Tuta but with Andabak.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So can you tell us precisely what Andabak did?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: He also took his pistol and shot the person in this person's head.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were these prisoners armed at the time that this occurred?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No. They had no weapons with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So after this second person was shot then, tell us what happened next.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: General Tuta approached a group. He selected ten people, and these people were then led away.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What's the next thing that you observed?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, I haven't seen anything. These prisoners were led away, and I haven't seen anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Who led them away?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The selected people from our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you hear anything after they were led away?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They were led into the ministry, and that is a small -- like part of woods and so, and you heard rifle gunfire.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were the women and the child among this group of people who were led away?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, the soldiers who led those people away, did you ever see them again?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. They returned afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What did they do after they returned?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: A few of them have started to drink something.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What did they tell you?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Nothing personally to me, because I would not command Croatian language that I could understand. I was just being translated by Zdenko.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What were you told?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That they had to shoot these people.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Simang, I'd like to ask you whether you at any subsequent time took part in any other military operations in the town of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Following this action?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, I did. Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately how much later this other action took place?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: There had been several operations directed at Mostar. I cannot tell you exactly at what time. It may be that I get mixed up with the months because I did not have any diary or any notes, and therefore, I cannot tell you when exactly which operations were in that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you recall any other operations in Mostar which you have not yet told us about today?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. There was one more operation which started at 12.00 noon.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And can -- well, first let me ask you. You've described two operations already in Mostar. Now, this operation which you say started at noon, can you recall if this operation occurred after the operations that you've already testified about?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: It must have been later. It was -- it was later, because all the operations which we've just described were right at the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you said that this operation started at 12.00, 12.00 noon. What was the objective of this operation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I was assigned to the Bofors, the 40 millimetre gun. We had to select a target. It was a position where we fired exactly at mosques at the Muslim side.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you receive any instructions or briefing prior to this operation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. We were given a sort of a map down in the ministry by General Tuta, and on this map, there was exactly marked which houses or mosques we should have to fire at, and accordingly, we should select our positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So tell us then what happened at 12.00 noon.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Sharp 12.00, the firing started.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you start firing on your own or did you receive an order?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The order came over Motorola.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And do you know who gave the order to you over the Motorola?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Judging by his voice, it was General Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, once you received this order, tell us what you did, how long the shooting lasted.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: This firing, this targeted firing, lasted for about five minutes, targeted firing, because we couldn't see anything afterwards because you had the smoke. All was embedded in smoke.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: So then after the firing stopped, what did you do?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, we continued firing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Were other members of the Convicts Battalion involved in this operation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. There were mortars there, then heavy artillery from the rear, all what was at our disposal.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know why 12.00 noon was selected as the time for this particular military operation?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. Muslims each time were prepared that we started normally early in the day, early in the day. And the second thing is that 12.00, people are in the mosques and have their prayers, so we could catch them at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: How did -- I think you said that you fired for some five minutes. Tell us what happened after that. How did the operation draw to a close?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, just when -- I did not say that we only fired for five minutes. I said we had targeted fire for five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Okay. Maybe you could explain that a little more. So then after five minutes, how did things change?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: After five minutes, you could not see the targets on the other side because everything was embedded in smoke, and so we fired blindly until the barrel was hot. And after then, we tried to withdraw. We reported about it to General Tuta. And when we tried to withdraw, we were fired at. We reported to General Tuta, and General Tuta then gave permission to withdraw.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, let me ask you -- I believe earlier in your testimony you mentioned a place called Ljubuski. I want to ask you have you ever been to Ljubuski and is there anything about Ljubuski which you associate with the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. In Ljubuski, there was a prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And do you know who was held at that prison?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Muslim prisoners were kept in that prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever go to that prison?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I have not been directly in the prison. I was in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What were you doing when you were in front of it?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I once participated in taking prisoners to this prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Are you able to recall where those prisoners came from?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: As far as I remember, either from Doljani or from Mostar, but I really do not recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know if any members of the Convicts Battalion took prisoners also to Ljubuski?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. There was a transport from Doljani to Ljubuski. I know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Do you know how the prisoners at Ljubuski were treated?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Nothing more -- nothing more precise is known to me. It's just hearsay.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'll ask the witness be shown Exhibits 25.5 and 25.6 at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Witness, you've had an opportunity to look at those two photographs. We can put 25.5 now on the ELMO. Do you recognise this place?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. That must be the new villa owned by General Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then we can put 25.6 on the ELMO. Is this also what you've called the villa of General Tuta?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever go to this place?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, I was there also.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: For what purpose did you go there?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I had a few questions to General Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you see other members of the Convicts Battalion there?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, his bodyguard, this Ivan. And then two or three other people were there, the names of whom I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. Simang, as we indicated at the beginning of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. your testimony, you're currently being held in a prison in a country that's not the Netherlands; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Can you tell us what is the reason, what are the crimes for which you were convicted that resulted in your being put into a prison?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I was (redacted) sentenced because I have shot at two soldiers of our unit by order, and I was reproached as having murdered them for reasons of robbing them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you've mentioned that you shot two soldiers of your unit. I want to ask you a couple of questions about the second of those two shootings, and if I understand correctly, we're talking about a person whose name was Biske; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And he was shot by you in August of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I do not know whether it was August, but it's true that I shot him.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Where did that take place?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: In the vicinity of Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And after that occurred, did you inform anyone of that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: After I shot the person, I personally reported it to General Tuta.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What did he say to you about that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: "I hope you have done it properly."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: What's the reason why you shot this person, Biske?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: He had stolen weapons and valuable objects from the barracks, from other comrades.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: After you informed Tuta that you had shot this person, what happened?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Approximately two to three weeks later, people from our unit came. We had to hand in weapons, and we were not allowed to leave Siroki Brijeg. It was said that from high above, that means obviously from Zagreb, that an investigation would take place about this shooting, about this killing.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Now, you say, "We had to hand in weapons." Who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: My then-captain, Ralf Mrachacz; Stephan Trupp, and Wolfgang Niederreiter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And these people that you've mentioned, Trupp and Niederreiter, who were they?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They were also soldiers in our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: You say you were not allowed to leave Siroki Brijeg. How long were you restricted there in Siroki Brijeg?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Approximately two to three weeks.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then what happened?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Then we went up to our base, and we were allowed to receive our weapons again.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Did you ever speak to Tuta again then at that point?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. Later when we would get in touch with him, we asked whether everything was okay for us, and the answer was, "Yes, everything is okay for you."

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: And then from that point forward, can you tell us approximately the period of time that you remained a member of the Convicts Battalion before you left Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: A few months still.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you. Cross-examination. Yes, Mr. Krsnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I am Defence counsel for the accused Mladen Naletilic and I have a few questions for you. I shall try to put my questions in such a way that I get the briefest and most concise answers possible from you. Also, please be so kind as to bear in mind the fact that everything that we are saying is being interpreted, so let us wait until we finish our respective questions and answers and then start speaking again. My first question, Witness, is: How many interviews have you had with the investigators or rather the Prosecutors of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Approximately four or five. I would not know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How did this happen? How come the investigators of this Tribunal came to see you?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Why, I do not know. Well, as I said, I was sentenced according to (redacted), and one day they were in the prison (redacted) .

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So you do not know how come they found out that you were in prison and why?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No. This is not known to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: (redacted), in addition to this verdict convicting you as a murderer and thief, you were also investigated for genocide; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No. I was not there for crimes of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My question was whether there was an investigation going on, not whether you were being tried.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. The federal attorney had made investigation for assisting in war criminals, but they had to be stopped since there was no satisfactory suspicion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: As for this joyous piece of news, did you write to Mr. Van Hecke about this, who is an investigator of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: This can be possible. I have sent several letters to Mr. Van Hecke.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know how many letters you've sent to Mr. Van Hecke?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I cannot say exactly. As mentioned before, I sent a number of letters.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you know Ralf Rudiger?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Ralf Rudiger Mrachacz, yes, I know him. He used to be my captain.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did he also write some letters to the investigators of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: This is not known to me, since Mr. Mrachacz was separate -- was in a different part of the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You don't have to give the name of the prison, but you were in the same prison, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you have no knowledge whatsoever of Mr. Mrachacz being in contact, notably in writing, with the investigators of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I do not know how many letters he has sent here. Nothing is known to me. He has never talked to me about it. I was in the hospital part for security reasons, and he was in a different part of the prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Do you remember, since it wasn't a long time ago, the 29th of June 1990, a letter that you wrote to Mr. Van Hecke?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter notes that Defence counsel did say 1990.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: There may be some confusion about the year. I heard 1990, and I think that it's not possible that there would have been correspondence in 1990.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Now I think there is some problem with the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Mr. Krsnik, would you please clear it up?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologize if there was a bit of confusion. It seems to me that I did say the 29th of June, 1999. Perhaps I omitted the last 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So it was 1999.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but as I said, I cannot remember dates. I do not have a diary, nor do I have any records, but it may be, because I have sent several letters to Mr. Van Hecke and to O'Brien or Rohde, and I do not know which letter you are referring to or alluding to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: By all means I shall remind you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But before that, in order to be fair, I'm not going to mention -- I'm not going to mention the name of the prison, but I think that all of us in this courtroom omitted to mention that the gentleman mentioned the name of the prison about ten minutes ago. He spontaneously admitted it himself, and it seems to me that everybody has failed to notice this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have had it redacted already. It won't appear in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Since we have the English version only, we don't have the German or Croatian versions, I assume that you wrote in the German language, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In the English version, this is how the letter reads: "Dear Mr. Van Hecke [In English] Mr. Reiser told me yesterday that my captain, Mr. Mrachacz, has written a letter to you." [Interpretation] Has this sentenced jogged your memory in respect of the rest of the contents of your letter?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. It's true Mr. Mrachacz may have told me at the door to the hospital ward that he was very angry and that for this reason he wrote a letter to the Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So my first question is: You did communicate with Mrachacz in prison, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. In the first prison, in the beginning, we used to have Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. contact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: My second question: Why was he angry?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Sorry, note of the interpreter: I did not get the full sentence.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Because nothing was done against the internment conditions, because we were threatened by prisoners coming from the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In this letter, did you apologise to Mr. Van Hecke because of the tone of Mr. Mrachacz's letters and the way he wrote them?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, that may well be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You were aware of the contents of that letter?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I did not know anything from Mr. Mrachacz. I was informed about it by the lawyer, Mr. Reiser.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Witness, how did your lawyer know what the other prisoner's letter said?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: -- object to the question. I think the witness is not in a position to know what his lawyer may or may not have known.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: That's reasonable. Mr. Krsnik, would you please skip this question. This sounds very strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise, Your Honour. I was just led by the witness's answer, and he said that he had been informed by his lawyer. So the logical question is: How can the lawyer be aware of what other prisoners wrote in their letters? I think that the question is more than logical. Your Honour, I am certainly going to tender all of these letters into evidence, and once they are read, I think that everybody will be quite clear as to what all of this is about. Never mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please be so kind as to tell me, Witness, you said "prison conditions." Did you get any promises from Mr. Van Hecke with regard to prison conditions?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The only promise I was given by the UN Tribunal or the investigation authorities that my life would be protected.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, in your letters both to Mr. Van Hecke and to the honourable trial attorney Susan Somers and to Mr. O'Brien - and we'll go back to the other names later - did you not condition your position not only by the transferral to another prison but also other matters? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Conditions? I'm sorry, but the condition was only that I will be protected and that I will be sent documents to prove clearly that I have acted on orders, and this is, as I said, not conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And what about your lawyer? Did he also contact the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal with regard to the same requests?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: My lawyer certainly got in contact with them, but I do not know whether he has set forward conditions. I don't think conditions -- what we were up to were that statements which I would make here, if there are also statements, that if there were statements made, as far as we are concerned, that we would be able to see or read such statements.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Didn't the lawyer extend his thanks twice, first of all because you remained in the prison hospital and second -- and the second time because through the Ministry of Justice of the Republic (redacted), the Office of the Prosecutor intervened on your behalf, to your benefit?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: This is beyond my knowledge, whether the Ministry of Justice has intervened. Of course, I have expressed my gratitude to the investigation authorities that I'm in security, as I have mentioned that I was threatened by prisoners from the former Yugoslavia, and this of course had also been written to the Ministry of Justice, and there is also a decision by court where you can read all this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Did you write a letter to a journalist who interviewed you when you appeared on television on his talk show, when you spoke about the events that you experienced in Bosnia? Did you write to him as well?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can remember, I have written to Sat 1 or Ulrich Meyer, if this is what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That's what I mean, yes. Did you also seek assistance from him, saying that, after that interview, you ended up in prison, or rather you wrote to him saying that in your letter?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Sorry, that was how the media had presented it, meaning that my statement during this TV show Sat 1, Einspruch with Meyer, that this was the starting point of other research which was carried out. And therefore I have said since he had kicked off all the further investigations, that he perhaps should also say what the conditions are in this prison.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You are giving me answers that are too extensive. I just asked you whether you wrote to him and whether you sought his assistance, nothing else.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Sorry. Yes, I have written.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, when you gave this interview, were you given money for it?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, I was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, during that talk show, did you say anything that led to the start of an investigation? Because the tape does exist.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: To my knowledge, I have not said anything with regard to investigation. I just mentioned that I knew of a person who I had shot dead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: That is Mr. Biske, right?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: To my knowledge, it was Heintz. That's the first one.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I beg your pardon, because you were tried for two murders.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, do you remember what you said during that interview on that talk show?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: With regard to what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: With regard to what you said during the talk show. I'm asking about that talk show. Do you remember it? Do you remember the questions and your answers?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. I approximately can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, did you speak similarly to the way you're speaking today or did you speak quite differently?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I spoke almost the -- in the same tone, if you referred to my relations to General Tuta. So please ask me whatever you mean, and if you ask me, I will tell you that General Tuta was almost like a father to us, and I still keep on saying this today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I don't want to lead you, really, because there is a videotape. I just wanted to ask you not only with regard to, as you had put it, General Tuta, but with regard to the Convicts Battalion in general.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, I do not know what you are alluding to, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: We'll go back to that. Tell me, how come you believe that Tuta is a general? Do you know that personally or did somebody tell you that?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, he was -- he was introduced to me as such, wherever it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Others introduced him to you as a general, and after that, you concluded that he was a general. Did I understand you correctly?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, since you spoke in German, did you socialise with everyone from the Convicts Battalion, as you would put it, or only people who came from the same area that you came from, the German-speaking area?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I got along very well with most of the people who were there, but of course, I had more to do with those people who spoke German.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Of course. The only question that comes to mind is: Could you talk at all to other soldiers without a translator?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No, very little.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Please be so kind as to tell me who was your immediate superior. Were you in a separate special unit within the Convicts Battalion? Did you have an immediate superior, an immediate commander?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No. It was mainly so that somebody who was there who knew German, Zdenko Ovlado, but otherwise we were on this Bofors, on the 40-millimetre gun, and there we had Maximilian Resch and a Croatian person.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: What was the name of this Croatian person?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: As far as I know, Branko.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And tell me, who commanded these Bofors?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Maximilian Resch.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, didn't you find it strange, although you did not have any military experience before that or, rather, is that correct, that you did not have any military experience before you came to Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Didn't you find it strange that a general would have meetings in cafes and issue directly orders to soldiers?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No, I didn't find it strange.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: You took that for granted or is that the way things actually happened all the time?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, I do not know. It was -- it seemed to be normal to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I see. And now tell me, if you had a commander, and if I understood you properly, it was that man called Resch who knew German. So tell me, how is it that nobody more or less than a general calls you directly, and even more than that, he issues orders, instructions directly to you, a plain soldier?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, as I said, since I do not know Croatian and Maximilian Resch neither did know Croatian, at least to the extent that we would understand Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. each single word.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, of course, Witness. That's why I'm asking you. But your superior, your immediate superior at the Bofors, he knows German. So if somebody is to be issued orders, shouldn't it be Mr. Resch, who speaks German?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Mr. Resch is a German, if you do not happen to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I think we're talking at cross-purposes now, so let me try to clarify it for you. In your testimony today, you said that a man whom you called Tuta knows German, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. He knows German perfectly, perfectly well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, then, my question is quite logical, because Resch speaks German, Tuta speaks German. And if he wanted to issue an order, as you are telling us all the time, then why didn't he call Resch on Motorola or at meetings if, that is, you had any meetings? Why did he speak to you?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: These orders came directly to the Bofors. Either I had the Motorola in my hand or Max would have it in his hand. And when the order came to Max, I was sitting next to him and I could hear everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, that's my question. Did they come to Max or did they come to you? Because you said today that you received those orders.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: It may be that I expressed myself not clearly. At any rate, the orders came from Tuta, as I could hear properly, because I could overhear the Motorola, as Max could. So when the orders came to Max, they were also valid for me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Thank you very much for this explanation. Now, tell me, who commanded the fire? I mean the Bofors.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The Bofors was under the command of Max.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please. Did Mr. Mrachacz, was he at the Bofors too?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Mr. Mrachacz was at the Bofors very seldom, maybe two times for the whole period. He was wounded, he was in rehabilitation because he was shot in his knee, and therefore, because of this wounding, he could not participate in a number of operations.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And he didn't even lend you a hand in those operations?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, as I said, he was there on one or two occasions and he handed up the grenades to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, when this thing with mosques happened, was Mrachacz on sick leave at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stringer?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: The witness has testified about mosques in a variety of locations. I just wonder if counsel could specify a bit more clearly which specific event he's asking the witness about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. That's a reasonable request. Mr. Krsnik, would you please clear it up?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I was about to do that. And of course I followed the logic of the answers, and I was trying to check it generally, but we can be more specific.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So the event that you described a little earlier of the mosque in Mostar, if I'm correct, was Mr. Mrachacz in hospital at the time or receiving treatment or on a sick leave?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, he was no longer in hospital. I think that was in April or in March when he was in hospital, when he was released from hospital, but I wouldn't be able to tell you exactly whether he joined us at the Bofors. I do not know exactly. I'm really sorry for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But that operation, when you were given the tasks -- task with mosque and everything, it was before April, it was in the very early days of the conflict, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I just said March or April, but I cannot tell you exactly. Please do not nail me down with months. I do not have a diary, and I cannot remember exactly which month it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: I'm not insisting that you tell me, but was it before Doljani, in any event? The operation that you described to us today, was it before Doljani? It's just to get some time references.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The mosques?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, the mosque in Mostar. Yes, the Mostar mosque. Was that operation that you described today, did it precede the operation in Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: You mean the 12 noon operation or what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yeah, the event that you described to the Prosecutor that the task you were given were to fire at the mosque. That is what you testified today, didn't you, if I'm correct? Yes, I think it was that operation at noon.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, that must have been after Doljani, if I remember correctly, but I'm not 100 per cent sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, a while ago you were not sure when you said that it was in March. I'm not insisting but then when did the operation in Doljani take place?

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Excuse me, I object to the last statement of counsel indicating that the witness said it was in March. My recollection of the testimony is that he said that he thought Mr. Mrachacz was released from hospital in March or April. So again I simply ask that we clarify precisely what we are talking about while we ask the witness about specific events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Krsnik, did you hear the objections from the Prosecutor? Better to have the picture more clear for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall be more than happy, Your Honours, because we also heard questions from the Honourable Court. We had questions from the Prosecution, and I'm simply trying to find where we are in time so that we could establish what time frame we are talking about, because my learned friend did not clarify fully that action which took place at noon, although the witness answered the Prosecution that it was in March or April, that is in the very early days of the conflict. And I merely wanted to say, since he mentioned Mr. Mrachacz, I wanted also to establish when could Mr. Mrachacz be there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you have the full right to make clear that time frame of that period. Just do not tell the witness that it's in certain month, like in March. We have to make sure what happened actually in March. I remember clearly the witness said "in March or April."

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, quite, Your Honour. The witness did say it was March or April, and I was merely trying to establish it with Simang. I never tried to put any words in his mouth. I simply tried to determine the time in relation to Mr. Mrachacz.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Just take it step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, by all means, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, Witness, you testified today about something that happened in front of the ministry. Could you give us the names of people who were there, of those 40? I think -- I believe you said 40. Could you give us some of those names, members of your battalion you were there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Krsnik, I hear there is 14, 1-4, rather than 4-0. Can you make it more clear?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I am at a loss now. It seems to me that I heard the witness say that it was about 40 men from his unit, but I really don't know. So we can ask.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: How many men were there from the Convicts Battalion in front of that ministry?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Maybe you are talking about the different groups of people, but you have a chance to make it clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe I already have done so, because I wanted to know how many members of the Convicts Battalion were there at the time. I had not yet broached the prisoners. I hadn't yet had time to come to the prisoners.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: I cannot -- I cannot tell you the exact figure. I have not counted the persons, how many would there have been. And to come back to your question as far as names are concerned, the names from our unit, with their normal civilian names, I do not know them. I even did not know that General Tuta's name was Mladen Naletilic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: But do you know their nicknames? Will you give me one nickname, at least, one name, the name of one soldier who was with you in front of the ministry? Was Cikota there? You already mentioned his name. Or Lija or ...

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: They were commanders. They were never with me. I was there in a group. And if I remember correctly, Vlado was there, and I do not know whether Zdenko was there. I do not know for sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, please, Zdenko, are you referring to Zdenko who was at the Bofors with you?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Correct. But as I said, I do not know for sure whether he was present there. Please do not nail me down on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, but in your testimony, you said that you spent quite a long time with that unit. You're talking about events which are not easily forgettable. So I'm asking you something very simple. Give me at least one name. You must remember the names of some people.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: As you said correctly, I do remember exactly the event, but I cannot tell you exactly who was there 100 per cent. I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Will you please be so kind as to list us the members of the unit that you call the Convicts Battalion, that is, those that you remember? Before that, tell me, please, your unit that was caught at that Heliodrom, was it also called the Convicts Battalion?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: At the Heliodrom there was the ATG.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: ATG, the Convicts Battalion, or was it only called ATG? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was only called ATG.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And that ATG is a part of the Convicts Battalion at Siroki Brijeg. Did they make that battalion? Is that what you are saying?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And together you were the sabotage unit, an intervention unit, or what?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes. We were called when fire was on somewhere.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you'd do your job and return; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. Now, tell me, please, so you were either on the front line or at Siroki Brijeg every day. Siroki Brijeg is a small place, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No, not necessarily. As I said in my statement today, when we had this green stage, we were allowed to leave Siroki Brijeg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. This is not what I wanted to ask you. Let's go back a little. I asked you all these questions trying to make you to give me at least five names or nicknames or anything of members of your unit at Siroki Brijeg or from this ATG, from what you call the ATG.

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, I know Commander Lija, Commander Baja, but as far as the soldiers are concerned, I am sorry, I just had Vlado, and Vlado is a person I had contact very often with, and I know Zdenko, but otherwise, I'm just sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you do not know any other names?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No. No other name would appear to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Tell me, Witness, how did you get to Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: We went to Doljani in a bus, in a VW bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And in that VW bus you arrived in Doljani directly?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No, at Masna Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Right. Now, will you tell the Honourable Court where is Masna Luka exactly?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Masna Luka is -- I do not know how many kilometres away from Doljani. I do not know how much. It is a place where there is these little dachas, that's these weekend houses, and we stayed overnight there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, we started ten minutes earlier. I do not know whether you intend to adjourn ten minutes earlier. Of course I have another seven minutes and I can go on, but because we started ten minutes earlier, I do not know what your decision is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We have six or seven minutes to go.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am being warned, so that is why I thought I better ask you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, tell me, if you remember, this Masna Luka, where is it?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, not far away from Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And how did you get to Doljani from Masna Luka then?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: The same, by VW buses and jeeps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Taking the road, I guess?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, these are not paved roads. It's sort of a rocky, shaky, country roads.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you fetched up in Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... fighting before you went to Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Fighting from our side?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No. I mean, was there any fighting? You arrived in Doljani, and there was no fighting, no combat?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: As far as I know, the Muslims had made an attack and they had shifted the lines, the border line there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: In Doljani?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: No, not in Doljani, in the surroundings of Doljani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Now, to make it quite clear, you fetched up in Doljani without any fighting. It was only from Doljani that you were to go to those front lines or what?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: How was that the first fightings or what? What did you say, the first fightings had been there without me being at Doljani? Or what did you really ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: No, no. I really don't know what the interpretation is, but when you say that the front lines had been moved. So it was from Doljani that you headed towards those front lines; is that it?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: This is how I was announced it. I was said that the front line had been shifted to the direction of Doljani, the Muslims had made a break-through, and for that reason we were supposed to go to Doljani. I have never said that I was sent to the front line. We have marched into Doljani because it was known or it was said to me that the Muslims had made an attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Well, that is precisely the answer that I wanted to arrive at by asking you all these questions. And now, tell me, please, which way did you take from Doljani? In which direction did you start from Doljani to arrive at the bunkers or ...

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Direction, Konjic, Jablanica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: And you again took the road to advance towards Konjic and Jablanica or -- no, to be more precise, my question is exactly where were the bunkers?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: In a piece of woods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: Next to the road?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Well, a bit away from the road, the main road, if you mean the main road.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat what -- the last sentence?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: One could not ride along or pass along on this main road there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: So if I understand what you are saying, the bunker that you headed for was in a forest or in a copse some way away from the road; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: FALK SIMANG
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRSNIK
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I see that 4.00 has passed and I have already rounded off this set of questions. I will, needless to say, continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: We will adjourn until 9.30 tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: 4.00 p.m., to be reconvened on Tuesday the 16th day of October, 2001, at 9.30 a.m.
